answer: One-way mutation clock. Each identity must replace its key each epoch by H(prev_key, epoch). Since clones share an identical prev_key, they produce identical keys, so the network rejects all but one. To forge a divergent key, an attacker must invert H to find a distinct pre-image, costing 2^n evaluations per fake identity per epoch. At the nadir of difficulty, this sets a minimum computational floor. A node's lantern, its signed history, proves unique temporal progression.
